In-flight writes that arrived under V+1-prepared but never observed commit are quarantined to a typed 'prepared-orphan-write' state on tenant_store and surfaced for operator review (likely re-played under V on rollback complete, but only under explicit decision rather than silent re-classification). Each abort writes a typed entry to compliance_audit.

stressors.description: A roster_version bump arrives at chain_router before tip_quorum (or vice versa). An in-flight M-of-N override proposal carries a credential that is valid under v_old but not v_new (compromised credential, scheduled rotation removal, etc.). Without a uniform cross-component invalidation ordering rule, the same proposal commits in chain_router (still on v_old) and is rejected in tip_quorum sub-zoom (already on v_new), leaving the system in an asymmetric override state — particularly bad when drain_coordinator force-complete consumes a chain_router-admitted override that tip_quorum would have rejected.
stressors.attractor: Without uniform invalidation ordering, the system is pushed toward override-state asymmetry: an attacker holding a credential being rotated out can race the rotation broadcast to commit a proposal in the laggard component while the leading component already rejects it. drain_coordinator force-complete is the worst case because the chain_router-side override may have already produced a state mutation that tip_quorum-side rejects ratifying, leaving the system mid-mutation under no valid override. Operator confidence in 'rotation invalidates immediately' is misplaced.
stressors.solution: Cross-component uniform invalidation contract on roster_version: every override-admission consumer (chain_router pool_membership_manager, tip_quorum sub-zoom, drain_coordinator sub-zoom, lifecycle_gate sub-zoom) treats roster_version monotonically AND the contract requires that an override proposal only commits if EVERY component it touches has an effective roster_version >= the proposal's signing roster_version at the same moment in HLC time. region_coordinator's credential_roster publishes rotation-prepare BEFORE rotation-activate (analogous to residency_publisher's 2PC): rotation-prepare collects ack from every override-admission consumer; rotation-activate is M-of-regions quorum-witnessed and consumers commit to v_new only on observing activation. In-flight proposals at the moment of activation are cancelled at every consumer (cancel-by-roster-version) atomically with the activation broadcast — a proposal whose signing roster_version < v_new is rejected at every consumer, even consumers that haven't yet processed the activation locally because they enforce the rule by consulting region_coordinator's currently-active roster_version on every commit. Per-component cancel-and-rollback semantics for in-flight proposals (already covered at zoom scope by r-s4-roster-revocation-propagation) compose with this at-root ordering rule.

stressors.description: A consumer (gateway, fanout, address_index, usage_meter, chain_router) restarts mid-apply of a lifecycle_gate-signed offboarding signal for tenant T. On replay, the per-tenant terminal-state must be reached at-most-once: drain-acks already issued cannot be retracted-and-re-issued, accounting records cannot be double-finalized, watch tombstones cannot be double-tombstoned (which would re-broadcast and tickle other consumers' dedupe by a stale (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id)). Without an explicit at-root idempotent-apply contract, double-apply could re-issue a drain-ack the consumer already retracted (breaking bubble-2's drain-fence contract from S3) or finalize counters twice.
stressors.attractor: Existing dedupe (r-s4-offboarding-signal-auth, bubble-region_coordinator-4) keys on (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id) but only ensures the consumer doesn't APPLY twice. It does not constrain the apply to be commutative-and-idempotent on terminal-state side-effects: a partial apply that wrote a watch-tombstone but not a drain-ack, on restart, could re-tombstone (a no-op locally but generates a duplicate compliance_audit entry) and then issue the drain-ack as if from a fresh apply. The result is two compliance_audit entries (typed offboarding-attestation) for the same (offboarding_id, component_id) which the certificate-of-deletion assembly cannot reconcile.
stressors.solution: Per-component idempotent-apply contract for HLC+nonce-keyed offboarding signals: every offboarding consumer maintains a durable per-(offboarding_id, component_id) apply-state record with a small set of typed phase-markers — RECEIVED, FLUSH-IN-PROGRESS, FLUSH-COMPLETE, ACK-EMITTED, ATTESTATION-WRITTEN, TERMINAL — that are written durably before each phase advance. On restart, the consumer reads the apply-state record and resumes from the last durable phase, never re-running an earlier phase whose side-effects are non-idempotent (e.g. compliance_audit attestation write is gated on ATTESTATION-WRITTEN being absent). The consumer NEVER retracts a drain-ack once emitted (no compensating action that creates a 'sometimes-ack-sometimes-not' state observable by tenant_store). compliance_audit's offboarding-attestation entries are keyed on (offboarding_id, component_id) for de-duplicating on the read side as a last-resort defense; consumers' ATTESTATION-WRITTEN phase-marker prevents the duplicate from being written in the first place.

stressors.description: A consumer (gateway, edge, usage_meter, metrics_store) cold-starts (or fails over to a fresh instance) into the middle of a residency policy_version transition. v8's sticky-deny-by-default + monotonic-per-(consumer, version) (r-s4-policy-ack-monotonic) means a fresh instance with no warmed ack history must deny everything for the publisher's freshness window. Worst case: a cold-start at the start of a tightening transition denies all traffic until the next ack window opens, which can be minutes — and during a region failover or scale-out event, MANY instances cold-start at once.
stressors.attractor: Without a pre-warm protocol, scale-out and failover events become correlated deny-storms: every cold-starting instance independently waits for residency_publisher's next ack window before serving residency-pinned traffic. Operator pressure under deny-storm is to disable the sticky-deny-by-default contract, which collapses the residency safety property. Alternatively, operators may pre-emptively ack-all-versions on behalf of the cold-start instance, which violates the per-(consumer, version) monotonic-ack contract (instance hasn't actually verified policy V) and creates ghost acks that persist past the fresh instance's actual readiness.
stressors.solution: Per-consumer pre-warm contract on cold-start: a fresh consumer instance, on registration with residency_publisher, requests a 'pre-warm hydration' that delivers the currently-active policy_version's full state synchronously; the consumer ack-readies the currently-active version inline as part of registration (not waiting for the next push window) and only AFTER ack-readying the active version does it begin serving residency-pinned traffic. The pre-warm hydration is treated by residency_publisher as an in-band ack from a fresh consumer instance and is rate-limited per-region to bound publisher load under correlated cold-start (scale-out) events. Pre-warm is a separate channel from steady-state push-and-acknowledge and does not bypass the monotonic-per-(consumer, version) contract: the hydration carries the active version and the consumer's instance_id (each instance has a distinct ack history). The pre-warm freshness budget is documented; if pre-warm cannot complete within budget the consumer falls to deny-by-default for residency-pinned operations and reports a 'pre-warm-stalled' state to operators.

stressors.description: A subpoena arrives months or years after the audit key for tenant T was destroyed. The certificate of deletion is itself verifiable (hash-chain intact, drain-acks present, DESTROYED log entry present) — but the per-store erasure attestations and per-tenant audit entries that the certificate VOUCHES FOR are encrypted under T's audit key and no longer decryptable by design. The compliance question: is the certificate-of-deletion sufficient as STANDALONE proof for the regulator/court, or does compliance_audit need to retain decryptable witness records on a SEPARATE key class (organizational key, not per-tenant) so that the structure-and-presence of the attested events remains inspectable post-shred?
stressors.attractor: If the certificate is the only artifact and per-tenant entries are unreadable, regulators may treat the certificate as a strong-but-opaque claim that cannot be independently inspected — pushing toward 'show me the records' demands that the system literally cannot satisfy. Conversely, if EVERY attested event is mirrored under a separate non-shred-able key, crypto-shred no longer guarantees tenant erasure (the entries' tenant-identifying fields are still readable on the witness key), defeating the purpose. The attractor is a blurred shred boundary.
stressors.solution: Two-tier audit material: (TIER 1, per-tenant key, shredded on erasure) — the full audit entry payload including tenant-identifying fields, request payload digests, signing-credential identities, and any other tenant-attributable detail; (TIER 2, organizational long-lived key, NOT shredded) — a structural witness of each attested event: event type (e.g. 'erasure-attestation', 'drain-ack', 'override-admission'), event HLC, originating component, and a hash commitment to the (now-shredded) Tier-1 payload. The certificate-of-deletion vouches for Tier-2 witnesses by verifiable hash chain; a regulator inspecting post-shred sees the structure-and-presence of every attested event in correct sequence, can verify the hash chain is intact, and can verify that each Tier-2 hash commitment matches what Tier-1 SAID was there (without seeing the tenant-identifying contents). Tier-2 contains NO tenant-identifying material so is not subject to erasure. The two-tier scheme is named at root; the per-tenant audit-encryption-key lifecycle remains a tenant_store zoom concern; the organizational long-lived key is part of the OOB-anchor key hierarchy under region_coordinator.

stressors.description: S3's drain-fence broadcasts are signed by lifecycle_gate; lifecycle_gate-signing credentials are roster-bound and may rotate mid-broadcast. If a broadcast began under v_old roster and the writer's ack arrives under v_new (because S9's rotation activated cross-component during the broadcast), are the acks still verifiable? If acks must be re-signed under v_new, has the drain window expanded past its HLC bound? Worst case interleave: a roster rotation activated to revoke a compromised signing credential lands during a bulk-offboarding storm; if revoked-credential-signed broadcasts retroactively become invalid, all in-flight drain-fences are unverifiable and writers cannot ack.
stressors.attractor: Without an interleave rule, the system is pushed toward one of three failure modes: (a) revoked-credential-signed broadcasts remain valid for in-flight drain-fences (the revocation is delayed for in-flight ops, breaking the 'compromise-revocation invalidates immediately' contract from credential_roster); (b) revoked-credential-signed broadcasts become invalid retroactively, all in-flight drain-fences are unverifiable, writers cannot ack, the offboarding HLC window expires under S5's retry budget, certificates of deletion finalize as erasure-incomplete or partial-with-witnesses; (c) re-sign in flight, but the re-signed broadcast has a different broadcast-emit-HLC and the per-tenant ack window calculation gets confused, S4's bounded-batching invariants are violated. None of these is acceptable.
stressors.solution: lifecycle_gate's drain-fence broadcasts are signed under a roster_version that is recorded in the broadcast itself; writers verify the signature against the broadcast's named roster_version, NOT against the writer's currently-cached roster_version. The signed broadcast is a self-contained credential bundle: writers may verify it for the duration of its HLC-bounded ack window even after a roster rotation has activated v_new, PROVIDED the signing credential at broadcast-emit-HLC was not subsequently revoked by COMPROMISE (scheduled rotation removal is not retroactively invalidating; compromise-revocation is). credential_roster's compromise-revocation event carries a 'retroactive-as-of-HLC' field — usually equal to the revocation HLC (no retroactive effect) but may be set to an earlier HLC when forensics establish compromise predates discovery; in that case in-flight broadcasts whose emit-HLC is at or after the retroactive-as-of-HLC become invalid and lifecycle_gate MUST re-sign-and-rebroadcast within S4's bounded-batching framework with a fresh broadcast-emit-HLC and a fresh per-tenant ack window. Every retroactive compromise-revocation is M-of-N-authorized at the elevated-issuance threshold and writes a typed entry to compliance_audit identifying the affected broadcasts.
